description: In full-motion mode (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, which is what most keyboard and screen-reader users have), none of the Contact controls can be reached with Tab until the visitor has scrolled the section into view. Every [data-reveal] wrapper starts as visibility:hidden (CSS, before hydration) and GSAP autoAlpha:0 keeps it that way until its ScrollTrigger fires. visibility:hidden elements cannot take focus. Measured on a fresh load: el.focus() fails on the mailto link, Copy, Download CV, LinkedIn and GitHub (5 of 5; computed visibility 'hidden'). Tabbing forward from the last Projects control ('VIEW WEBSITE ↗') goes straight to the footer's 'BACK TO TOP ↑' and skips all five, both at 1440 and at 375. Scrolling to the footer only then fires the reveal, after focus has already passed. The screen-reader tree for #contact at that point is just the h2: the intro paragraph, email, CV and social links are all missing. These are the page's main calls to action. Fails WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard (A), 2.4.3 Focus Order (A) and 1.3.1 (A). The existing audit missed it because capture.mjs prime() scrolls the whole page before the keyboard and axe passes.
suggested_fix: Never use visibility:hidden as the pre-reveal state. Change the CSS to `html.js [data-reveal]{opacity:0}` and animate `opacity` (not `autoAlpha`) in Reveals.tsx (default: fromTo {opacity:0,y:40} → {opacity:1,y:0}; stagger: from children {opacity:0,y:32}). Content then stays in the accessibility tree and focusable. Also add a `focusin` listener on each [data-reveal] (or document-level) that calls `tween.progress(1)` / `scrollTrigger.kill()` so a focused, still-transparent element becomes visible at once (2.4.7).

description: The footer clock re-renders every second forever (setInterval 1000 ms), including when prefers-reduced-motion is set (measured 17:29:17 → 17:29:18 in the reduced-motion context). There is no pause or hide. It is auto-updating content presented in parallel with other content, which is what 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A) covers, and the seconds digit is a constant flicker in peripheral vision. description: This concerns the Copy fallback in the working tree, which runs when navigator.clipboard is missing. It uses `field.select()` on a readonly textarea but doesn't call `setSelectionRange(0, len)`. It also leaves the textarea at its default font size (<16px), with no top/left. iOS Safari doesn't select text from `select()` alone, so `execCommand('copy')` can still return true and show "Copied ✓" even though nothing was copied. Focusing a field smaller than 16px can also trigger iOS auto-zoom. If everything fails, the address is selected with no message, which on iOS shows no callout. The desktop simulations pass: Chromium and WebKit with navigator.clipboard removed both show "COPIED ✓", with scrollY unchanged and scale 1. Real iOS is the unverified case, and it's the owner's own LAN test path.
suggested_fix: In fallback(), set `field.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;top:0;left:0;opacity:0;pointer-events:none;font-size:16px'`, then call `field.focus({preventScroll:true}); field.select(); field.setSelectionRange(0, field.value.length)`. On failure, switch the pill to a visible hint (e.g. "Hold to copy") rather than only selecting the address.

description: The custom cursor hides the OS pointer for everyone with a fine pointer, with no opt-out. html.has-cursor *{cursor:none!important} removes the user's enlarged or high-contrast system pointer and replaces it with a 6px paper dot plus a ring that lags by 0.45s. The dot is 1.19:1 against white surfaces and the ring (paper at 35%) is 2.84:1 on ink. With forced-colors active, the cursor still activates (QUERY ignores forced-colors): the dot keeps background rgb(255,255,255) on the white Canvas, and the ring is forced to black, so it vanishes over black text. The real pointer is effectively lost.
suggested_fix: Extend QUERY with 'and (forced-colors: none) and (prefers-contrast: no-preference)'. Better: don't set cursor:none; draw the ring as an addition to the native pointer, so the OS pointer and its accessibility settings always survive.

description: Dragging the window's bottom edge (a height-only resize, which arrives as many small resize events) throws the reader out of the section they were reading. The guard in SmoothScroll compares each resize event with the previous one and returns early whenever the width is unchanged and the height moved less than 150px, so a slow vertical drag never sets `resizing` and the refresh handler never restores the anchor. Every section above the reader is sized in vh (hero 170/190vh, statement 220vh, Focus height = slide distance + innerHeight), so the content moves but the scroll offset does not. Measured, all at Experience row 3 / Contact / Clarté / Skills: 1280x900→560 in 20px steps: the reader ends in Contact with the row they were reading 2037px above the viewport top (single-jump 900→560, Δ340 ≥150, keeps it exactly: row top 80px, so only the stepped drag fails). 1440x900→780 in 15px steps at the Contact heading: heading ends at -346. 1100x760→640 at the Clarté card: card heading at -1157, 'This website' now on screen. 900x960→840 at the Skills heading: -331. Crossing the Focus height thresholds (580/700) vertically is the worst case because Focus also switches between horizontal and stacked. Width drags and rotations are fine (measured 1440→1150 in 30px steps, 1024x768↔768x1024, 1100x650→1300x650: all kept within 30px). Expected: the same place-keeping as for width changes; the 150px tolerance is only meant to ignore phone toolbar resizes.
suggested_fix: Compare against the size recorded when the anchor was last taken, not against the previous resize event (keep `anchorSize` alongside `anchor` and update it in onRefresh), so a drag of many small steps still adds up past the threshold. Better: only apply the 150px tolerance on touch devices (`matchMedia('(hover: none)')`), where it exists for the address bar; on a pointer device treat every height change as a resize.

description: The hero gate — the page's signature motion and the first thing anyone sees — runs well under 30 fps on desktop, and the cost is rasterization, not JS. Method: scroll #top from 0 to its full height at a steady 260 px/s with a rAF loop, recording every frame gap, then repeat with one layer disabled at a time (same run, same machine). 1440, CPU 4x: median frame 35.1 ms (28 fps), p90 38.9 ms, 64% of frames over 33 ms (repeat run: 35.8 ms, 72%). 1440 with NO CPU throttle it is barely better — median 34.2 ms (29 fps), 62% long frames — so this is not a slow-CPU artifact. 1920, CPU 4x: median 54.8 ms (18 fps), p90 60.9, 70% long frames. Attribution, 1440 unthrottled, median frame / % frames >33 ms: base 34.2 / 62% → hide .grain 30.1 / 15% → kill the .hero-circuit-mask two-gradient mask 28.1 / 1% → hide .hero-floor 24.3 / 2% → hide the whole .hero-circuit-scroll layer 20.5 / 1%. The dominant cost is that .hero-circuit-mask (two mask-image layers composited with mask-composite: intersect) sits INSIDE the element the scroll timeline scales from 1 to 1.7, so a viewport-sized masked SVG is re-rasterized on every frame of the gate; .hero-floor (a perspective-transformed bg-grid under a linear-gradient mask, scaled 1 → 1.25) is second; .grain (a fixed 1760x1220 noise layer stepping 5x per 0.9 s) is third. Adding will-change:transform,opacity to all four scroll layers does NOT help (median 35.4 ms, 68% long) — confirming the work is raster, not compositing. Every other section on the page is clean at the same throttle (median 16.6-16.8 ms, 0 long frames), so the hero is the page's only janky scroll.
file_line: components/hero/Hero.tsx:105-110 (scale on .hero-circuit-scroll / .hero-floor-scroll / .hero-glow-scroll); app/globals.css:224-230 (.hero-circuit-mask, mask-composite: intersect); app/globals.css:195-204 (.grain); components/hero/Hero.tsx:194-200 (mask nested inside the scaled wrapper)
suggested_fix: Move .hero-circuit-mask off the scaled node and onto the outer, unscaled .hero-circuit-scroll wrapper (the vignette is a viewport effect and should stay put while the circuit zooms through it), so the scale becomes a pure composited transform over an already-rasterized texture. Same for .hero-floor: put the mask-image on .hero-floor-scroll rather than inside it. Then hide .grain for the duration of the gate (it is decorative and already switched off on touch). If any one of those is too invasive, killing the double mask alone takes long frames from 62% to 1% in these measurements.
confidence: high on the relative attribution (repeated three times, monotonic and consistent across 1440/1920 and throttled/unthrottled); medium on the absolute fps, since headless Chromium rasterizes on the CPU and a real GPU will do better
verified_evidence: vfps 1440 hero gate: worst frame 83ms → 50ms, 46.8 → 48.3 fps (headless CPU raster; mask moved off the scaled layer)

description: The slideshow's push-in is on a 5 s clock that matches no slide's length, so it never lands, and at the handover it visibly reverses. .slide animates transform with `transform 5s linear` from scale(1.04) to scale(1). Measured by sampling the computed matrix of every .slide each frame for 16 s at 1440: a still slide is shown for 4183 ms, so at handover its scale is still 1.0065 — it has covered 84% of its 0.04 travel and is cut off mid-creep, never resting at its designed size. The scroll slide is shown for 9014 ms: its scale reaches exactly 1.000 at the 5 s mark and then the frame is completely motionless for the last 4.0 s while the capture glides underneath. Worse at the handover: the outgoing slide is at 1.0065 (or 1.000) and immediately starts growing BACK toward 1.04 at the same linear rate, so for the 800 ms the crossfade is still visible (opacity 0.42 at +100 ms, 0.07 at +300 ms) the leaving frame is zooming the opposite way from the arriving one. `linear` is also the only linear easing in an element-state transition anywhere on the page — every other one uses --ease-out-expo.
file_line: app/globals.css:619-629 (.slide, transform 5s linear) with components/projects/Slides.tsx:19-23 (STEP_MS 4200, SCROLL_MS 8000, MAX_GLIDE 12) and :49-51 (the computed `duration`)
suggested_fix: Drive the push-in from the slide's own clock instead of a fixed 5 s: set `transitionDuration: `${duration}ms`` inline on the active .slide alongside the existing animationDuration on the progress bar, so the zoom lands exactly when the slide hands over whether it is a 4.2 s still or a 9 s scroll slide. Reset the outgoing slide's transform without a transition (transition-duration: 0 on :not(.is-active)) so it cannot reverse under the crossfade, and use var(--ease-out-expo) or a gentle ease-out rather than linear.
note: push-in runs on the slide clock

description: One event, four different speeds. When the copper spark reaches an anchor, everything that is supposed to 'power on' from that single moment runs on a different clock: .trace-pad 0.5 s, .section-index box-shadow 0.9 s, .xp-org / .xp-dates colour 0.9 s, .chip-corner 1 s, .chip-box border 1.2 s and box-shadow 1.4 s, .xp-row::before underline 1.4 s, .contact .accent text-shadow 1.4 s. Measured at 1440 by stepping the scroll at a steady 600 px/s through #experience and timing, per element, from the class flip to the visual end state: the pad's glow is at full 14 px blur 166 ms after the flip (mean of 7 pads, range 165-168 ms), while the same row's copper underline needs 883 ms to reach scaleX 1 (mean of 6 rows, range 881-884) — a 5.3x spread for two things triggered by the same spark passing the same point. So each Experience row snaps a pad on, then drifts its dates copper, then sweeps an underline, as three separate events rather than one.
suggested_fix: Give the power-on family one duration token (e.g. --dur-power: 0.9s) and use it for every property that answers the spark, keeping a deliberate offset only where one is meant to trail the other (the underline sweep can stay longer if it is also given a small transition-delay so it reads as a consequence of the pad rather than a parallel animation).
note: --dur-power 0.9s for every property that answers the spark

description: Scroll reveals are on a fixed 1.2-1.4 s clock with only 12% of a viewport of runway, so at a brisk scroll they finish long after the element has arrived — and on `stagger` groups the last child lands after the group has left the top of the screen. Method: constant-velocity rAF scroll of the whole page at 1440, sampling each frame, recording where each [data-reveal] element sat when its tween started and where it sat when it settled. At 900 px/s (a normal flick-and-read): every plain reveal starts with its top at 84-86% of the viewport and settles ~700 ms later with its top at 8-13% — it crosses about 75% of the screen while still fading in. `stagger` groups are worse because the trigger is the container: they start at 61-71% and settle with the container top at -2 to -4% of the viewport, i.e. the last chips in Skills and the last rows in the About datasheet finish arriving after they have scrolled off the top edge. At 400 px/s the same reveals settle with their top at ~51%, which is the intended feel — so the effect is entirely scroll-speed dependent and there is no compensation.
file_line: components/motion/Reveals.tsx:26 (start 'top 88%', once), :39 (lines duration 1.4), :52 (stagger duration 1.2, stagger 0.08), :62 (default duration 1.3)
suggested_fix: Either shorten the reveals to ~0.8-0.9 s (still on-brand with the expo.out family and the 1.2 s gsap default) or lower the trigger to 'top 95%' so the element has a full 20-25% of viewport of runway before it is needed; for `stagger`, set the ScrollTrigger on the container but start it from the container's own top with a small negative offset so the tail children are not staggered off-screen.
confidence: high on the measurements; medium that the current timing is wrong rather than a deliberate choice
note: reveals 0.9s (lines 1s, clip 1.1s)

description: The grain layer keeps a permanently promoted compositor layer where its animation is switched off. .grain declares `will-change: transform` unconditionally, but the `grain` keyframes are cancelled under both `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and `(hover: none)`. Measured at 390: getComputedStyle(.grain).animationName === 'none' while willChange === 'transform', so a 710x1164 fixed layer (inset:-160px, i.e. viewport plus 320 px each way) is held promoted for an animation that will never run — on the devices least able to spare the GPU memory. At 1440 the same layer is 1760x1220 = 2.15 Mpx; a full inventory of the page at the top of the scroll finds 18 promoted elements totalling 6.51 Mpx, of which .grain is the second largest after the 783x3424 scroll capture already filed as UI-197.
file_line: app/globals.css:195-204 (.grain, will-change: transform) with :215-219 (@media reduced-motion, (hover: none) { .grain { animation: none } })
suggested_fix: Move `will-change: transform` out of the base .grain rule and into a `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) and (hover: hover)` block so it is declared only where the animation actually runs — or drop it entirely, since the keyframes already use translate3d and will promote the layer on their own while playing.
note: grain promoted only where it animates

description: Opening the mobile menu puts the focus ring on an item that is still moving, and closing has no counterpart to the staged open. Measured at 390 by sampling the panel's opacity and each .menu-item's translateY every frame: on open the panel reaches opacity 1 at 310 ms, but the four items are at y = 42, 48, 48, 48 px at t=11 ms and the last one does not settle until ~610 ms — and Nav.tsx focuses the first link synchronously in the same tick, so the copper 2px focus ring is drawn on a link that then travels ~42 px under it. On close the panel simply dissolves: opacity 0 at 183 ms, display:none at 299 ms, with the items left at y=0 the whole time. So opening is a 610 ms staged reveal and closing is a 300 ms flat fade with nothing staged — a 2x asymmetry with no shared gesture.

description: Flow 1 (recruiter, laptop), step 'clicks View website' on the first project card: the flagship CTA is a dead end. There is no guest mode, no demo account and no way back except the browser's Back — and the link opened in a new tab, so Back there goes nowhere. description: Flows 4 and 5 (French visitor / returning visitor): the first-visit intro replays in the middle of a reading session. The head script marks the session 'booted' when `location.hash` is present (app/[locale]/layout.tsx:70), but only Boot's own onComplete writes sessionStorage `gs-booted` — and Boot bails out early when the class is already there (components/Boot.tsx:18-21). So anyone who arrives on a shared section link never gets the flag set. Repro A: open /en#projects fresh (measured: lands at Projects, sessionStorage gs-booted = null), read a while, scroll up and click FR. Expected: the French page at Projects. Observed: the full boot splash covers the screen for 2.7s with the page scroll-locked (is-locked true from t=319ms to t=3050ms), and only then does it open onto Projects in French. Repro B: open /en#projects fresh, click the logo (which clears the hash to /en), then reload — the same 2.7s splash, again with scroll locked. The visitor has been on the site for minutes and is shown the 'first visit' animation, twice over, each time losing control of the page.
file_line: app/[locale]/layout.tsx:70 (bootScript sets 'booted' from location.hash but never gs-booted); components/Boot.tsx:18-21
suggested_fix: Write the session flag wherever the intro is declared over, not only when the timeline finishes: in the head script, `try{sessionStorage.setItem('gs-booted','1')}catch(e){}` on the same branch that adds the `booted` class, and in Boot's early return. Then a deep-link arrival counts as the visit it is.

description: Flow 5 (returning visitor), step 'Back/Forward between sections': the address bar walks the page but Back does not. Clicking About, Projects, Experience, Contact in the header takes the address through /en#about -> /en#projects -> /en#experience -> /en#contact (verified, each landing on its section), yet history.length is still 2 — scrollToTarget uses history.replaceState, so none of the four clicks leaves a history entry. Expected after four section clicks: Back steps back through the sections, or at worst does nothing. Observed: one Back press leaves the site entirely (about:blank in the test; the referring page, e.g. LinkedIn, in real life). Forward then returns to /en#contact at y=14518, which proves the address really was the navigation state the whole time. The same applies to the phone menu links. Combined with flow 1 (where 'View website' opens a new tab, so Back there is a no-op too), a visitor has no working Back anywhere in the journey: every press is a one-way exit.
suggested_fix: Use pushState for the four header/menu section links (keep replaceState for the logo's #top and for anything the page does on its own), and add a popstate listener that scrolls to the hash without re-pushing. The reader's place is already restored on back_forward navigations, so the section anchors are the only missing piece.

description: Flows 3 and 5, step 'Back to top': the address is left pointing at the section the visitor just left. The footer button calls scrollToTarget(0) with a number, and the `history.replaceState` branch in lib/scroll.ts only runs for string targets starting with '#', so the hash is never cleared. Measured: click Contact in the nav (address /en#contact, y=14518), click 'Back to top' (y=0) — the address still reads http://localhost:3000/en#contact while the reader is looking at the hero. The header logo does the same journey via scrollToTarget('#top') and correctly clears it to /en, so the two controls for 'go to the top' leave two different addresses. It matters at the next step: reloading from there lands at the top (the saved-place restore wins) while the address still says #contact, and anyone who copies or bookmarks that URL shares a link to Contact for a page they were viewing from the top.
suggested_fix: Make the footer button call scrollToTarget('#top') like the logo does, or clear the hash in scrollToTarget when the target is the numeric 0 — either way the two 'back to top' controls should end on the same address.

description: All six flows, the whole scroll-through: below lg the page gives no sense of where you are or how much is left, on a document that is 22.6 screens long (measured 19067px at 390x844; 15958px / 17.7 screens at 1440x900). Three things that would normally answer 'where am I' are all absent or switched off: (1) no header or menu link is ever marked current — all four keep aria-current=null and the same text-mute class at every scroll position (measured across a full 30-step scroll); (2) the address never changes while scrolling — the URL stayed exactly '/en' through About, Focus, Projects and Experience, so the only way to get a section address is to click a nav link; (3) the one progress cue, the copper meter, is `hidden lg:block` and aria-hidden (components/motion/ScrollProgress.tsx:35), so phones, tablets, every landscape phone and screen-reader users get nothing. The result on a phone is 20+ screens of scrolling with no landmark other than the section headings themselves, and no way to tell whether the end is near.

Updating the address with replaceState as sections pass would fix the 'copy the link to this section' case at the same time.
note: progress meter now renders at every width, on the mirrored rail

description: Flow 3 (keyboard-only), the Shift+Tab return trip: the focus ring goes missing for about half a second every time focus moves up a long distance, while the same move downward is instant. Measured from the Lead Finder slide steps (settled at y=8396) pressing Shift+Tab once to the hero's 'Download CV': the browser's own scroll-into-view is overridden by Lenis's lerp, so scrollY eases 7681 -> 3323 -> 1077 -> 231 -> 19 -> 0 and the focused button sits at top=-6083, then -1725, before it first appears on screen at ~600ms and settles at ~1.5s. Expected: the control that just took focus is on screen when it takes it. Observed: 500ms with the focused control off screen and no ring anywhere, then a 1.5s glide. Tabbing forward over the same distance (hero -> Projects, ~8000px) lands in one frame with the button already at top=575, so the two directions behave differently for no reason the visitor can see. In the full Shift+Tab run back up the page this happened twice in a row (indices 17 and 18 of 27).

description: Flow 2 (phone), step 'rotating to landscape mid-way': turning the phone sideways makes the project screenshots smaller and less readable, not bigger, and leaves almost half the screen empty. description: The datasheet's barcode has 20px of empty track baked into its own box, so the card's footer row does not end on the card's right padding edge. The <svg> is viewBox='0 0 64 24' drawn at h-6 w-16 (exactly 1:1, 64x24 CSS px), but the bar loop only advances to x=44: the widths [2,1,3,1,1,2,1,3,2,1,1,2,3,1,2,1,1,3] with `x += w + 1` place the last painted rect (i=16) at x=43 w=1, and the odd-index entries are never rendered. Measured at 1440: the card runs 56 -> 556, its px-5 content edge is 535, the header strip's 'GS-26' part number ends at exactly 535, the barcode's <svg> box also ends at 535 — but the last bar's ink ends at 515. So the barcode reads as floating 20px (31% of its own width) inside a justify-between row, ragged against the part number directly above it. Same 20px at every viewport because the svg is not fluid.
suggested_fix: Make the viewBox match the ink the loop actually draws: compute the total advance (sum(widths)+gaps = 44 with the current array) and use viewBox={`0 0 ${total} 24`}, or drop the trailing gap and pad the array to fill 64. Keep w-16 so the drawn width is unchanged; only the empty right track disappears and the last bar lands on 535 with GS-26.
note: barcode viewBox 44x24

description: The outlined marquee words use a fixed 2px -webkit-text-stroke while the type scales from 32px to 72px, so the optical weight of the outline more than doubles between phone and desktop. Measured: font-size 32px at 375 -> stroke 0.0625em; 38.4px at 768 -> 0.0521em; 72px at 1440/1920 -> 0.0278em. At 375 the 2px stroke on 32px caps nearly closes the counters of 'AI' and reads as heavy as the solid words' stems; at 1440 the same words are a delicate hairline outline. The solid/outline contrast the band is built on therefore inverts by viewport. The same fixed-stroke problem sits on .footer-mark (1px at 65.6px type at 375 = 0.0152em, vs 336px type at 1920 = 0.0030em, a 5x relative swing), and the two members of the same 'outlined word' motif use different widths (2px vs 1px).
suggested_fix: Set the stroke in em so it tracks the optical size: `-webkit-text-stroke-width: 0.028em` on .marquee-outline and `0.004em` on .footer-mark (matching what they already look like at 1440/1920), or clamp() it per breakpoint. Then the outline reads the same weight at 32px and 72px, and the two outlined-word treatments agree.
note: stroke 0.028em

description: The lit copper rail — the page's signature 1px line — never renders crisp, because a 1.5px stroke is centred on an integer x. railX() returns Math.round(gutter/2) = 28 at 1440, and CircuitTrace draws the core path at strokeWidth 1.5, so the ink spans 27.25-28.75 CSS px.
